title: Polynomial target evaluation of the presentation-pair derived colimit
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $E$ be a set, and put $C=B[E]$, the polynomial $B$-algebra on $E$. Choose a common infinite cardinal bound containing these rings and variable sets and small representatives as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the opposite of the category of compatible diagrams $A\to P\to Q\to C$, $P\to B\to C$, where $P$ is polynomial over $A$ and $Q$ is polynomial over $P$; morphisms before taking opposites are commuting pairs of $A$-algebra maps on $P,Q$ preserving both augmentations. Let $\mathcal D$ be the opposite category of polynomial $B$-algebras $T$ with a $B$-algebra augmentation $T\to C$, with augmentation-preserving $B$-algebra maps before taking opposites. Give both the topology generated by singleton identity coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Define $v:\mathcal P\to\mathcal D$ by $v(P,Q)=(Q\otimes_P B\to C)$. For any commutative ring $R$ and any $R$-module presheaf $F$ on $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $L\pi_{\mathcal P,!}^R$ and $L\pi_{\mathcal D,!}^R$ be the derived colimits represented by [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. The canonical augmentation
$$L\pi_{\mathcal P,!}^R(v^{-1}F)\longrightarrow F(C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}C)[0]$$
is an isomorphism in $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It is the composite of the canonical reindexing map to $L\pi_{\mathcal D,!}^R F$ and the augmentation induced by the arrows $(C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}C)\to(T\to C)$ in $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top); module coefficient version via sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\mathcal P^{op}$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal D^{op}$. A presheaf is a covariant module functor on the corresponding non-opposite category. The bar theorem identifies the stated derived colimits with derived colimits on these small categories. To use the simplicial-computation theorem, identify its first-vertex bar convention with the bar theorem's last-vertex convention: their differentials in degree $-n$ differ by $(-1)^n$, and multiplication by $\lambda_n=(-1)^{n(n+1)/2}$ is a chain isomorphism since $\lambda_n=(-1)^n\lambda_{n-1}$. This is the identity in degree zero and commutes with every reindexing map and augmentation. Work in these identified models. Choose the standard polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ supplied by the resolution-coherence theorem, within the fixed size bound, and set $U_n=(P_n\to B,P_n[E]\to C)$. Each is an object of $\mathcal A$, and extending every simplicial operator by the identity on $E$ makes $U_\bullet$ a simplicial object. Transport to the chosen small representatives by isomorphisms when necessary.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), first paragraph; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08Q9, with the explicit bar sign identification.

proof.text: The resolution-coherence theorem says that every $P_n\to B$ is surjective and $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For constant $B$, the alternating differential is zero in odd positive chain degree and the identity in even positive degree, so $s(\operatorname{const} B)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore $s(P_\bullet)\to s(\operatorname{const} B)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Applying the surjective-quasi-isomorphism criterion to the underlying simplicial abelian groups proves that $P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const} B$ is a trivial Kan fibration, with the boundary lifting property and vertex surjectivity of the cited definition.

The map $P_\bullet[E]\to\operatorname{const}(B[E])$ is also termwise surjective and a quasi-isomorphism on alternating complexes. Indeed let $\mathcal M=\mathbf N^{(E)}$ be the set of finitely supported monomial exponent functions. Coefficients identify its underlying simplicial abelian-group map with $\bigoplus_{m\in\mathcal M}(P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const} B)$, because simplicial operators act on coefficients and fix all variables. The alternating complex is the same direct sum of complexes. A cycle in a direct sum has finite support and is a tuple of coordinate cycles; a boundary is a tuple of coordinate boundaries. Choosing preimages only on that finite support proves $H_n(\bigoplus C_m)=\bigoplus H_n(C_m)$. Thus Step 2 gives the required homology isomorphisms. Termwise surjectivity follows by lifting the finitely many coefficients of a polynomial. Apply the same surjective-quasi-isomorphism criterion. This proves the trivial Kan fibration needed for the top polynomial algebra, including infinite $E$, without a filtered-colimit preservation theorem.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), last paragraph, expanded by the finite-support coefficient argument; simplicial.tex Tag 08P1 (lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups).

proof.text: For $W=(P\to B,Q\to C)$ choose polynomial coordinates $P=A[S]$, $Q=P[T]$. A simplex of $X_W=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(W,U_\bullet)$ consists precisely of elements $x_s\in P_\bullet$ over $\beta(s)$ for $s\in S$, and $y_t\in P_\bullet[E]$ over $\gamma(t)$ for $t\in T$: the second algebra map extends the first and is determined freely by the $y_t$. This coordinate description commutes with all faces and degeneracies. A boundary lifting problem for $X_W\to *$ is therefore a family of boundary lifting problems for the maps in Steps 2 and 3 over the indicated constant simplices. Fill each coordinate, choose the fillers for the sets $S,T$, and extend uniquely by the polynomial universal property. Vertex lifts are obtained in the same way. Consequently $X_W\to *$ is a trivial Kan fibration by the cited definition, and the homotopy-equivalence theorem makes $X_W$ homotopy equivalent to a singleton. Empty generator sets give empty products, hence a singleton; infinite generator sets cause no restriction because each chosen coordinate defines an algebra map out of a free polynomial algebra.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), representable mapping simplicial sets; simplicial.tex Tag 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy).

proof.text: Apply the simplicial derived-colimit computation to $\mathcal A$, the coefficient functor $v^{-1}F$, and $U_\bullet$. Step 4 verifies its representable-contractibility hypothesis, so it gives an isomorphism $a_U:s(F(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}L\pi_{\mathcal P,!}^R(v^{-1}F)$. Here $vU_n=P_n[E]\otimes_{P_n}B\simeq B[E]=C$, canonically by the maps fixing coefficients and variables; all operators become identities. In $\mathcal B$, the augmented algebra $(C\xrightarrow{1}C)$ is terminal: the unique augmentation-preserving map from $T\to C$ to it is the augmentation of $T$. Its constant simplicial object therefore has singleton representable mapping sets. The same theorem gives $a_C:s(F(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}L\pi_{\mathcal D,!}^R F$. Apply its reindexing naturality to $v^{op}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, identity coefficients, and the displayed simplicial isomorphism $v^{op}U_\bullet\simeq\operatorname{const} C$. It says $c\,a_U=a_C$, where $c$ is the canonical reindexing map. The bar theorem and Step 1's signs identify this $c$ with exactly the reindexing map in the statement. Hence $c$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution), applied to both categories; Tags 08PG and 08PH, reindexing map; cotangent.tex Tag 08QV.

proof.text: Write $M=F(C)$ and let $\epsilon_{\mathcal D}:K_{\mathcal D}(F)\to M[0]$ be the augmentation whose degree-zero component at $T$ is restriction along $C\to T$ in $\mathcal D$. The maps form a cocone, so this is a chain map. Let $i:*\to\mathcal B$ pick $C$, with coefficient $M$ on the one-object category. Apply the simplicial-computation theorem there to its constant unique object, obtaining an isomorphism $a_*:s(M)\to\mathbf H(*,M)$. Its reindexing naturality gives $a_C=\mathbf H(i,1)a_*$. On bars, $\epsilon_{\mathcal D}\mathbf H(i,1)$ is exactly the augmentation $\epsilon_*:K_*(M)\to M[0]$, since the only degree-zero image is $(C,x)\mapsto x$. This augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism: the constant alternating complex has differential zero in odd degrees and identity in positive even degrees; its degree-zero section and the homotopy $h_n=1$ for odd $n$, $h_n=0$ for even $n$ contract it to $M[0]$. Thus $\epsilon_{\mathcal D}a_C=\epsilon_*a_*$ is an isomorphism. Since $a_C$ is an isomorphism, so is $\epsilon_{\mathcal D}$. This argument applies also to $M=0$ and to any coefficient ring $R$.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), evaluation at C; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 08PG, 08PH and 08Q9, reindexing from the one-object category.

proof.text: Finally $\epsilon_{\mathcal D}c$ is exactly the requested augmentation. In degree zero its bar generator $(W,x)$ maps to $(vW,x)$ and then to the restriction of $x$ along $C\to vW$. In higher degrees both augmentations to $M[0]$ are zero. These are equal chain maps; the sign identification of Step 1 does not alter them in degree zero. The arrows $C\to vW$ are natural because both sides of their naturality square are the augmentation of the polynomial $B$-algebra in the non-opposite category. Thus the stated canonical map, with its stated factorization, is the composite of the two isomorphisms proved in Steps 5 and 6, and is an isomorphism in $D(R)$.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), explicit augmentation and reindexing formula.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-c1010485a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full. The statement is unchanged and identical to the live node, which is still unsplit. There are no new nodes and no cycle (312-node closure without the item), and no SGA source is used. I checked the item against Stacks 08QV, whose route it follows: U_n=(P_n,P_n[E]), contractible Hom(W,U_•), then the 08Q9 computation. Step 1: the sign λ_n=(-1)^{n(n+1)/2} correctly matches the last-vertex bar convention of the bar node with the first-vertex convention of the computation node, and size stays within the cardinal bound. Step 2: the coherence node gives termwise surjectivity and the quasi-isomorphism; s(const B) has differentials 0/1, so 08P1 makes P_•→const B a trivial Kan fibration. Step 3: P_•[E] is a direct sum of copies of P_• indexed by finite-support monomials, which replaces Stacks' filtered-colimit lemma and is valid for infinite E. Step 4: a morphism (A[S],P[T])→U_n is the same as coordinates x_s over β(s) and y_t over γ(t), so lifting reduces to fibrewise lifts, and 08NS then gives contractibility. Step 5: C→C is terminal in D^op, vU_•≅const C, and the reindexing clause gives c a_U=a_C. Step 6: ε_D H(i,1)=ε_*, the constant complex contracts, so ε_D is an isomorphism. Step 7: the composite is the stated augmentation. I tested E empty, infinite E, A→B non-surjective or non-flat, R=0 or F=0, and empty S or T; nothing breaks. Accepted tool_use: lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence (sk-prop-h2, which the unit does not cite) as a generic 08NS black box. Route pivot: def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration is the classical 08NL definition, used at Steps 2 and 4 for lifting; 'simplicial set' means the classical Hom-simplicial sets of 08Q9, not dropped ∞/model-category machinery. I accept both.
